To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) the “low-voltage field emission” is a phenomenon of the field emission from the surface of the 2D nanosystem of the type: A conductor — a thin dielectric film; 2) this phenomenon is caused by the presence of a thin dielectric (insulating) film on the surface of a metal conductor; 3) the “lowvoltage field emission” phenomenon is a consequence of the field-induced charge separation in the dielectric film; and
the low voltage emission is a result of the field enhancement in the nanostructures.

the “low-voltage“ field emission from a two-dimensional nanoheterostructure surface of a kind “a conductor – a thin dielectric film” is caused by the presence of a thin dielectric layer (a dielectric film) on the surface of the conductor.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the field emission properties of nanometer-scale structures.

the development of the phenomenological theory of the field emission from a nanosystem of a kind: a conductor — a thin dielectric film, which has been experimentally investigated in [1–5] and is known as a low-voltage field emitter.
a new type of field emission from a nanoheterostructure of a conductor — a thin dielectric film.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the “low-voltage“ field emission from a two-dimensional nanohetero-structured surface of a type: a conductor — a thin dielectric film is the result of a combination of two factors: a) the presence of a thin dielectric dielectric film on the surface of the conductor, b) the presence on the surface of nanosize conductive inclusions.

the low-voltage thermal field emission from 2D nanosystems of the kind: a conductor — a thin dielectric film is a result of a combined action of the following factors: the field enhancement effect of a nanosystem, the effect of a thin film dielectric layer, the effect of the field emission of the nanosystem, and the effect of thermal emission of the nanoheterostructure surface.

the low-voltage field emission is a phenomenon of the field electron emission from the nanoheterostructures, where the nanosize effect is the most significant, and the field emission is the most effective.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the “low-voltage field emission” is a result of the interaction between a conducting substrate and a thin dielectric layer on the surface of a nanostructure.

the model of the “low-voltage field emission from the 2D nanosystem” is based on the following: 1) the existence of the 2D electron states of the conduction electrons on the surface of the conductor (the 2D electron gas); 2) a thin dielectric film (the thickness of which is of the order of the characteristic length of the electron states in the 2D gas) is placed on the surface of this conductor; 3)
the “low-voltage field emission” is a consequence of a specific field emission properties of 2D nanosystems.
The main takeaway from our work is that
in the case of a nanoheterostructure, the emission current is determined not only by the work function of a material of a conductor but also by the dielectric constant of the dielectric layer.

the field emission current is caused by the tunneling of electrons from the conduction band of the conductor into the conduction band and/or the valence band of a thin dielectric film and, in the case of a dielectric film with an electron affinity less than the electron work function of the conductor, by the tunneling into the conduction or valence band of the conductor.

the “low-voltage field emission” phenomenon is a result of a combination of two processes: (i) field emission from the surface of nanostructures of a conductive material, and (ii) tunneling through the dielectric layer, which covers the surface of nanostructure.
